question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Lineage-resolved, time-stamped AP-1 reporter tracing: Build an inducible, lineage-tracing system (e.g., a Cre- or Dre-recombinase reporter driven by AP-1-responsive enhancers) that permanently marks cells that experienced a transient AP-1 pulse, then wash out the stimulus and track whether marked cells retain altered chromatin or transcription after days to weeks. Persistence in marked cells after the stimulus is removed, without ongoing AP-1 activity, would be direct evidence of memory.
2. Acute AP-1 degradation or inhibition during the memory window: Use an auxin-inducible degron (or a dominant-negative c-Jun/Fos or a photo-controllable AP-1 inhibitor) to remove AP-1 at defined times: during the stimulus, after the stimulus, and during re-stimulation. If AP-1 is a true memory mechanism, the altered chromatin state or primed gene response should persist when AP-1 is removed after induction, but be lost when AP-1 is removed during the initial pulse or the reactivation step.
3. Chromatin persistence profiling (ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, H3K27ac) across a stimulus-washout time course: Profile AP-1 occupancy (c-Fos/c-Jun CUT&RUN) together with chromatin accessibility and histone marks at multiple timepoints after a transient stimulus and after a second stimulus. Testing whether enhancers that were bound by AP-1 during the pulse remain open or marked after AP-1 leaves the chromatin distinguishes genuine epigenetic memory from simple ongoing transcription.
4. Re-stimulation kinetics and priming assays: Compare the transcriptional and AP-1 binding response to a second identical stimulus in naive versus previously stimulated cells, measuring the speed, amplitude, and gene set of the response (e.g., by time-resolved RNA-seq or live single-cell reporters). Faster or stronger re-induction of the same target genes in primed cells, and dependence of that priming on the original AP-1 pulse, would support a memory function rather than a simple dose response.
5. Mechanistic dissection of the memory determinants with targeted perturbations: Combine targeted epigenome editing (dCas9-based writers/erasers such as p300 or LSD1 fused to AP-1-bound loci) with mutations in the AP-1 binding motifs and in putative self-reinforcing partners (e.g., BAF complex, bromodomain proteins) to test which features are necessary and sufficient for persistence. Showing that a chromatin mark at a single AP-1-bound enhancer can by itself reproduce or abolish the memory effect would establish a causal mechanism rather than correlation.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and sister-cell inheritance of a primed state
ideas.description: Use HaloTag-tagged c-Jun or c-Fos with single-molecule tracking through mitosis to test whether AP-1 stays on mitotic chromosomes after a pulse, then compare re-induction kinetics between sister cells that inherit the same pulse history. If the primed state is inherited by both sisters without ongoing AP-1, that supports bookmarking-based memory rather than a per-cell state that resets at division.

ideas.title: Nucleosome turnover pulse-chase at AP-1-bound enhancers
ideas.description: Express SNAP-tagged H3.3 (or H2A.Z) and measure nucleosome exchange rates at AP-1-bound versus unbound enhancers during and after a transient stimulus using pulse-chase labeling and ChIP-seq. A memory mechanism would predict that enhancers retaining a primed state show slower nucleosome exchange that persists after AP-1 leaves, which is distinct from simply measuring whether the chromatin mark is present.

ideas.title: Protein-lifetime readout of AP-1 memory using fluorescent timers
ideas.description: Knock in tandem fluorescent timers (or FAST-tagged versions) to JunB, ATF3, and c-Jun to measure the age and half-life of the chromatin-bound AP-1 pool after a stimulus, and pair this with cycloheximide chase and phospho-proteomics. If a long-lived, chromatin-bound AP-1 protein pool or stable post-translational modification predicts the duration of the response, memory may be stored in protein turnover rather than in a chromatin mark.

ideas.title: Enhancer-promoter loop persistence after pulse by Micro-C
ideas.description: Perform Micro-C or HiChIP on AP-1 target loci at multiple time points after a transient pulse, and test whether loops that formed during stimulation persist after AP-1 is gone and after the promoter is transiently silenced with CRISPRi. Loop persistence that is independent of transcription would point to 3D genome architecture as the memory substrate, something that ATAC or histone-mark profiling cannot detect.

ideas.title: Information-theoretic quantification of memory capacity
ideas.description: Deliver AP-1 pulses varying in duration, amplitude, and spacing, then use single-cell reporter readouts at several later times to estimate the mutual information between pulse history and the subsequent response. A genuine memory mechanism should carry information about the past beyond what a simple decaying dose-response model predicts, and this can be tested by comparing against a fitted null model that uses only the current AP-1 level.
